note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §11, §13.7, Stage 45) on data/benches/boiling.json: boiling's bubbles. Heated from below, the beaker's floor stands far hotter than its water; bubbles of steam start there, rise, and condense in the cooler water a fraction of a millimetre up; as the water nears its boiling point they climb higher, and at the boil they reach the surface (lab/bubbles.hpp).
title: Experiment: bubbles of a boil

steps.title: A burner under the beaker
steps.text: Pick up the burner in the cabinet, then click the beaker.
steps.why: The beaker holds 200 g of water, 5.9 cm deep. A flame heats its floor; the water takes the heat from the floor.

checks.text: the burner is under the beaker

steps.title: Full flame
steps.text: Right-click the burner to choose it, then drag its valve fully open.
steps.why: About 450 W through a floor of 34 square centimetres. Warm water rises off the floor and the cooler sinks onto it, so the water stays near one temperature; the floor itself stands far hotter.

steps.title: A monitor on the bubbles
steps.text: Drag a monitor out of the parts drawer onto a free square. Drag from its sensing port onto the beaker. Click "vessel", then "bubbles' height".
steps.why: Where the floor is hot enough, a scratch in the glass holds a speck of steam, and it grows into a bubble: about 2.3 mm across as it leaves the floor. The monitor reads how high the bubbles get before they are gone.

checks.text: a monitor reads how high the beaker's bubbles reach

steps.title: Above 5 cm
steps.text: Click "above". Then click the value, type 5, and click "set".
steps.why: Its lamp lights once the bubbles reach nearly to the surface.

steps.title: They climb
steps.text: Click 10x on the clock. Point at the beaker: the readout says how far the bubbles get. Watch the cloud of them low in the water.
steps.why: A bubble of steam in water cooler than its own boiling point gives its heat to the water and shrinks: in cold water it is gone a fraction of a millimetre up, in water a kelvin under the boil after a centimetre or two. The heat it carried warms the water all the same.

steps.title: The boil
steps.why: At the boil the water is as hot as a bubble's own steam, nothing condenses it, and the bubbles reach the surface: the steam leaves the water. Its floor boils a little hotter than its surface (the water's weight on it), so the bubbles still shrink a little low down.

checks.text: the water at 99.5 C or more

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged
